svg.text: FIG 03: MAXIMUM POWER TRANSFER THEOREM: DC PROOF, VARIABLE ELEMENT TRAP & 7-CASE AC MATRIX
Calculus Derivations • Operating Point Shortcut • Active Loads • 50% Efficiency Limit • Complete 7-Case AC Complex Conjugate Matching

g.text: 1. DC MPTT Derivation & Efficiency
The Maximum Power Transfer Statement (DC)
In a linear DC active network, a VARIABLE load resistance R_L connected across
the terminals will absorb MAXIMUM power from the source IF AND ONLY IF
the load resistance equals the Thévenin resistance of the driving network:
R_L = R_th (Optimum Power Condition)
Crucial Constraint: Network parameters (V_th, R_th) must be FIXED!
Rigorous Calculus Proof via First Derivative
Load current: I_L = V_th / (R_th + R_L). Power dissipated in load R_L:
P_L(R_L) = I_L² · R_L = V_th² · [R_L / (R_th + R_L)²]
Differentiating P_L with respect to variable load R_L and setting to zero:
dP_L / dR_L = V_th² · [ (R_th + R_L)² - 2 R_L(R_th + R_L) ] / (R_th + R_L)⁴ = 0
(R_th + R_L) · [ (R_th + R_L) - 2 R_L ] = 0
R_th - R_L = 0 ⟹ R_L = R_th (Q.E.D.)
Maximum Power Delivered to Load:
P_max = V_th² · R_th / (2 R_th)² = V_th² / (4 R_th)
In terms of Norton short-circuit current: P_max = (1/4) · I_sc² · R_th.
Terminal voltage at max power: V_L = V_th / 2. Terminal current: I_L = I_sc / 2.
Efficiency & The 50% Power System Barrier
Total power generated by source at maximum power transfer condition:
P_gen = V_th · I_L = V_th · [V_th / (2 R_th)] = V_th² / (2 R_th) = 2 · P_max
Efficiency Calculation at Maximum Power:
• Exactly HALF the generated power is WASTED as heat inside the source (R_th)!
Engineering Philosophy Distinction:
✓ Communication / RF / Sensors: Maximize signal transfer (MPTT applied, η = 50% OK).
✗ Power Systems / Grid Transmission: NEVER operate at MPTT! (Operating at 50% efficiency
would melt generators and double fuel costs; power grids operate at R_L ≫ R_th, η > 95%).
Classroom Drill: Power vs. Load Curve Shape
Behavior of P_L as R_L varies from 0 to ∞:
• At R_L = 0 Ω (Short Circuit): V_L = 0 V ⟹ P_L = 0 W, η = 0%
• At R_L = R_th (Peak Optimum): P_L = P_max = V_th² / 4R_th, η = 50%
• At R_L = ∞ Ω (Open Circuit): I_L = 0 A ⟹ P_L = 0 W, η = 100%
Symmetry of Sub-Optimal Operating Points:
For any target power P < P_max, there exist EXACTLY TWO distinct load values
R_L1 < R_th and R_L2 > R_th that absorb the same power P!
Geometric Mean Invariant: R_L1 · R_L2 = R_th²
Example: If R_th = 10 Ω and R_L1 = 5 Ω gives 10 W, then R_L2 = 100/5 = 20 Ω gives 10 W!
2. THE MASTER TRAP: Variable Internal R
THE #1 DEADLIEST TRAP IN NETWORK THEORY
GATE Question: "Find the value of resistor R to transfer maximum power to a FIXED
load resistor R_fixed = 10 Ω."
The Fatal Student Error (90% of Candidates Fail!):
Blindly applying MPTT and setting R = 10 Ω !
Mathematical Reality & Calculus Truth:
MPTT applies IF AND ONLY IF the LOAD is variable and the SOURCE is fixed!
When the LOAD IS FIXED and the INTERNAL RESISTOR IS VARIABLE, MPTT DOES NOT APPLY!
The 3 Canonical Scenarios of the Variable Trap
Scenario 1: Variable Resistor R in SERIES with Source (V_s, R, R_load fixed):
P_load(R) = I² · R_load = [ V_s / (R + R_load) ]² · R_load
To maximize P_load, we must minimize denominator (R + R_load):
Optimum: R = 0 Ω (Short Circuit!) [P_max = V_s² / R_load, η = 100%]
Scenario 2: Variable Resistor R in PARALLEL / SHUNT with Source:
Resistor R shunts away current from the load branch.
To maximize power reaching the load, R must divert ZERO current:
Optimum: R = ∞ Ω (Open Circuit!)
Scenario 3: Variable Resistor R IS THE LOAD ITSELF (Standard MPTT):
Here the target power is dissipated inside variable element R itself:
P(R) = [ V_th / (R_th + R) ]² · R
Optimum: R = R_th (MPTT Strictly Valid!)
Notice the stark difference: R = 0 Ω vs R = ∞ Ω vs R = R_th!
Active Load Matching (Resistor in Series with Source E)
What if the load branch contains an active voltage source: Load = R_L + E_L?
DANGER: Do NOT set R_L = R_th blindly! Load is not a pure passive resistor.
The Operating Point Principle (Faculty Method):
To maximize power absorbed by the ENTIRE active load branch:
V_terminal = V_th / 2 and I_terminal = V_th / (2 R_th)
Match the load terminal equation V_L(I_L) to the operating point directly:
E_L + I_terminal · R_L = V_th / 2 ⟹ Solve for R_L !
Exam Diagnostic Decision Matrix
Q1: Which element is variable? ⟹ If load → MPTT. If internal → Calculus/Limits.
Q2: Where is power measured? ⟹ In variable element? Or fixed element?
Q3: Is the load purely passive? ⟹ If active source present → Operating point!
Follow this 3-question diagnostic to avoid all negative marks in GATE!
3. AC Circuits & Reactance Tuning
AC Power Definitions & The Active Power Law
In AC sinusoidal steady-state (phasor domain), source has Thevenin impedance:
Z_th = R_th + j X_th (R_th > 0, X_th can be inductive + or capacitive -)
Load impedance: Z_L = R_L + j X_L.
CRITICAL LAW: AC Load Power is ALWAYS Active (Real) Power:
P_L = |I_L|² · R_L (in Watts [W])
• Pure reactances (L, C) have zero average power dissipation: P_reactance ≡ 0 W!
• DANGER: Never calculate P_L = |I_L|² · |Z_L|! (That gives Apparent Power S in VA).
The Universal AC Load Current & Power Equation
Total loop impedance: Z_total = (R_th + R_L) + j(X_th + X_L).
Magnitude of load current phasor:
|I_L| = |V_th| / √[ (R_th + R_L)² + (X_th + X_L)² ]
Average Active Power Delivered to Load:
P_L(R_L, X_L) = |V_th|² · R_L / [ (R_th + R_L)² + (X_th + X_L)² ]
The Reactance Cancellation Principle:
• In the denominator, (X_th + X_L)² is a squared term (≥ 0).
• If X_L is independently adjustable, we can minimize denominator by setting:
X_th + X_L = 0 ⟹ X_L = -X_th (Series Resonance!)
Peak vs. RMS Source Specification Trap
THE EXAM DISASTER: Confusing Peak (V_m) with RMS (V_rms)
If the source is given as a time-domain waveform: v_s(t) = V_m cos(ωt + ϕ):
RMS Voltage: V_rms = V_m / √2
Maximum Power Formulas Compared:
Using RMS Voltage: P_max = |V_th,rms|² / (4 R_th)
Using Peak Voltage: P_max = V_m² / (8 R_th) (Factor of 8!)
• In GATE NAT questions, using V_m² / 4R_th instead of V_m² / 8R_th loses 2 marks!
• ALWAYS check if source amplitude is specified as Peak or RMS!
Tuning Components for Reactance Cancellation
To achieve X_L = -X_th in practice at frequency ω (rad/s):
1. Source is Inductive (X_th = +ω L_th > 0):
Load must be CAPACITIVE: X_L = -1 / (ω C) = -ω L_th
C_optimum = 1 / (ω² · L_th)
2. Source is Capacitive (X_th = -1 / (ω C_th) < 0):
Load must be INDUCTIVE: X_L = +ω L = +1 / (ω C_th)
L_optimum = 1 / (ω² · C_th)
At this resonance point, power factor = 1.0 (Unity), circuit behaves purely resistively!
4. The Master 7-Case AC MPTT Matrix
CASE 1: Both R_L and X_L Independently Variable
Complex Conjugate Matching Condition:
Z_L = Z_th* = R_th - j X_th
(R_L = R_th and X_L = -X_th)
Maximum Active Power Delivered:
P_max = |V_th|² / (4 R_th)
The gold standard: Both resonance and resistance matching achieved simultaneously!
CASE 2: R_L Variable, but X_L is FIXED / CONSTANT
Here reactance cannot be tuned to zero. Differentiating P_L with respect to R_L:
R_L = √[ R_th² + (X_th + X_L)² ]
SPECIAL SUB-CASE 2A: Purely Resistive Load (X_L = 0 Ω):
R_L = |Z_th| = √(R_th² + X_th²)
DANGER: NEVER set R_L = R_th when X_th ≠ 0 and load is pure resistor!
P_max = |V_th|² · |Z_th| / [ (R_th + |Z_th|)² + X_th² ]
CASE 3: X_L Variable, but R_L is FIXED / CONSTANT
Since R_L is fixed, power is maximized purely by minimizing loop impedance:
X_L = -X_th (Cancel source reactance!)
P_max = |V_th|² · R_L / (R_th + R_L)²
(If R_L happens to equal R_th, this collapses to Case 1: P_max = |V_th|²/4R_th).
CASE 4: Fixed Load Angle θ_L, Variable Magnitude |Z_L|
Load power factor cos θ_L is constant (Z_L = |Z_L| ∠θ_L), but magnitude can vary:
|Z_L| = |Z_th| = √(R_th² + X_th²)
• Magnitude of load impedance must equal magnitude of source impedance!
Generalizes Case 2A (where θ_L = 0°) to any arbitrary fixed load phase angle.
CASES 5, 6 & 7: Tuned Elements & Constant Current
CASE 5: Tuning Capacitor C to Maximize Load Power:
ω L_th = 1 / (ω C) ⟹ C = 1 / (ω² · L_th)
CASE 6: Tuning Frequency ω for Fixed L & C:
ω_res = 1 / √(L · C) (Resonance Frequency)
CASE 7: Constant Current Load I_o:
• Load draws fixed current I_o regardless of terminal voltage.
• Power absorbed: P_L = V_terminal · I_o = (V_th - I_o · R_th) · I_o.
• Maximize by making R_th as small as possible (ideally R_th = 0 Ω)!
Master Mnemonic for AC MPTT:
"Tune reactances to CANCEL (-X_th); match resistances to EQUAL (R_th)!"
